text: hey everybody the Bible is not a univocal text that is simply a fact that does not speak with a single consistent and unified voice and one of the most
significant implications of that is that any attempt therefore to extract from the Bible a single consistent or unified message or principle or moral or ethical
or even legal framework is the product of negotiation it is the product of deciding which passages are going to be
centered and prioritized and which passages are going to be marginalized subordinated and reinterpreted if not outright ignored that's simply an
inevitability of engaging the Bible as an authoritative text and there's nothing wrong with that in and of itself but it can become a problem if people
convince themselves that it is not a negotiation and particularly when they do so in the deployment of the Bible as
a rhetorical bludgeon or weapon against minoritized marginalized or oppressed groups like The lgbtq plus Community or
women or racial minorities and these negotiations are overwhelmingly driven by a desire to structure power and
values in the service of a given group's identity politics which means that the harm and the oppression and the
marginalizing of those groups continues because it's useful to those groups for it to continue and it's entirely up to
them when they will decide that the value of those lives exceeds the value of the Bible as an identity marker in
that structuring of power and values
